section_1.title: Intuitive Hook: The Velocity-Position Analogy
section_1.content: Introduce the concept of a robotic rover moving along a path. Explain that if we know the 'rate of change' (velocity), we can determine position via accumulation (integration), and if we know the 'total position,' we can determine velocity via change (differentiation).
section_1.example: A Mars rover moving forward: Its speedometer gives us the derivative (velocity), while the total distance recorded on its odometer represents the integral (accumulation).

section_2.title: Prerequisite Review: Slope vs. Area
section_2.content: Visually define the derivative as the slope of the tangent line (rate of change) and the integral as the area under the curve (accumulation). Show an animation of a tangent line sliding along a curve vs. a vertical bar sweeping across an area.
section_2.example: Visualizing a graph of f(x)=x^2; the derivative at a point is the steepness of the curve's slope, while the integral from 0 to x is the shaded area under the curve.

section_3.title: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus (Part 1)
section_3.content: Explain that differentiation and integration are inverse operations, much like addition and subtraction. If you integrate a function and then differentiate it, you return to the original function.
section_3.example: Applying the operator: Start with f(x) = x^2, integrate to get (x^3)/3, then differentiate to return to x^2. Show this as a circular 'undo' motion in the animation.

section_4.title: Synthesis: The 'Accumulation Function'
section_4.content: Define the accumulation function F(x) = ∫[a to x] f(t) dt. Explain that the rate at which this 'accumulated area' grows is exactly the value of the function f(x) itself.
section_4.example: A water tank filling up: The volume of water (the integral) increases; the rate of that increase (the derivative) is equal to the current flow rate of the faucet.

section_5.title: Summary & Takeaway
section_5.content: Conclude that differentiation decomposes total change into local rates, while integration reconstructs total change from local rates. They are two sides of the same coin.
section_5.example: A quick visual recap: A 'Derivative' magnifying glass zooming in to see local change, and an 'Integral' glue stick assembling pieces to see the total picture.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (6x6 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1.0 # 0.5 to 5.5
                y = 2.2 - i * 1.0 # 2.2 to -2.8
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Review: Slope vs. Area", [

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
